description: Small, authored retrieval exercise on research methodology. Each passage is independent and each question has one or more relevant passage IDs.

passages.control: Randomly assigning participants to treatment and control groups reduces systematic differences between groups before treatment.
passages.blinding: Masking group assignments from the people rating outcomes limits observer bias during evaluation.
passages.bootstrap: Bootstrap resampling draws repeated samples with replacement. The variation across estimates can be used to form a confidence interval.
passages.recall: Recall divides the count of retrieved relevant records by the count of all relevant records. It measures completeness of search.
passages.precision: Precision divides the count of retrieved relevant records by the count of all retrieved records. It measures the purity of a result list.
passages.ablation: An ablation experiment removes one component while keeping the remaining system fixed to estimate the contribution of that component.
passages.leakage: When near-duplicate records appear in both training and validation partitions, measured performance can be inflated by data leakage.
passages.latency: A latency benchmark records elapsed request time and reports quantiles including the median and the ninety-fifth percentile.
passages.agreement: Cohen's kappa compares agreement between two independent annotators with the agreement expected by chance.
passages.stratify: Stratified sampling draws observations from each defined subgroup, maintaining coverage of rare groups.

questions.text: How do I quantify the useful fraction of returned hits?
Which metric detects relevant documents our search has missed?
How should I test the effect of disabling the reranker alone?
Why might almost identical train and test examples distort validation accuracy?
How can we measure whether two human labelers agree beyond coincidence?
How can I estimate uncertainty through sampling with replacement?
How can an experiment limit bias when assigning treatments or scoring outcomes?
What measurements capture the long tail of response times?
How do we ensure a small subgroup is included in the sample?
